replace.check_task: Read the environment-owned faithful LIBERO task result. Use when: physical and visual evidence suggests the requested task may be complete, and always before finish_episode(outcome=success). Effect: read-only; it queries the only policy-visible official task checker. Returns: task_success when the checker is available, or a retryable task_checker_unavailable result. Does not: change the world, explain why the task passed or failed, expose the hidden predicate, or substitute for physical verification during manipulation. On error: Refused: any argument (invalid_arguments). Wait for the Runtime to expose the checker and retry; never infer official success from tool or motion success.
replace.compute:
Calculate derived quantities from numbers already available to you.
Use when: before using a newly calculated number to choose or parameterize an action, call compute. This includes a single offset, distance, angle, unit conversion, quaternion calculation or residual check. Send the expression before using its answer; do not substitute mental arithmetic. Batch related calculations when useful. No call is needed to copy an already returned valid value, reuse a result whose inputs and assumptions are unchanged, or choose a constant that requires no calculation. For image, depth or calibration queries, use geometry_query; use mark_point when a current pixel measurement needs a persistent name or cross-view check.
Selection examples: deriving a new world target by adding an offset to a measured point -> compute, then use the returned point. Locating a known world target in a camera image -> geometry_query(world_points_m=...). Copying a valid planner pose unchanged -> the selected motion or execution tool, with no redundant calculation.
Ready to use: np, Rotation, math, geom, pi, float and int are prebound; do not write import statements or function definitions. bindings is a list of {name,value,from?}; numeric lists become arrays automatically, so b-a works directly. Each call starts fresh: pass every input again. Use Rotation.from_quat(q).as_matrix(), Rotation.from_euler('xyz', angles, degrees=True).as_quat(), np.linalg.norm(v), np.clip(x,-1,1), and math.radians(degrees) directly. Quaternions are [x,y,z,w].
Geometry helpers: geom.unit(v) normalizes a nonzero 3-vector; geom.angle_deg(a,b) returns the unsigned angle in [0,180] degrees without hand-written normalization or acos; geom.rotate(q,v) rotates a 3-vector by q; geom.transform_point(t,q,p) returns t + rotated p. The translation and rotated point must share the declared destination frame and units. Helpers use only your inputs; they do not choose the correct frame or robot axis. unit and angle reject zero directions and use scaled normalization to avoid overflow/underflow.
Call format examples (replace these illustrative numbers with your inputs):
{"bindings":[{"name":"a","value":[0.1,0.2,0.3]},{"name":"b","value":[0.4,0.6,0.3]}],"expressions":"distance_m = np.linalg.norm(b - a)","outputs":["distance_m"]}
{"bindings":[{"name":"p","value":[0.1,0.2,0.3]},{"name":"q","value":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0]}],"expressions":"axis = geom.rotate(q, [1, 0, 0])\npoint = p + 0.03 * axis\nangle = geom.angle_deg(axis, [0, 0, 1])","outputs":["point","angle"]}
The first example returns distance_m=0.5; the second returns point=[0.13,0.2,0.3] and angle=90. expressions is one JSON string; encode line breaks as \n, with no Markdown fences, imports, print or return statement. A final bare expression is available as result.
Effect: read-only pure calculation, no robot decision, scene read, image, files, network or persistent state.
Returns: outputs entries with name, value and kind. Set outputs to the final variable names you need (or result for the last expression); temporary arrays are then not serialized or counted as returned measurements. Omit outputs for the historical automatic numeric-variable results. Unreturned working values are named in intermediates_not_returned. Numbers are rounded to nine decimal places.
Does not: measure the world, detect stale inputs, prove reachability, contact, retention or task success. A computed value remains conditional on your measurements, units and assumptions. Only the listed numeric namespace is available; module loading and general Python are unavailable.
On error: Refused: a block beyond the Limits below; a construct outside the evaluator grammar; an unknown, reserved or underscore-prefixed name; a string literal longer than 32 characters; a binding whose from is blank or longer than 120 characters; an output name the block never assigned; a non-finite result, or no numeric result at all. Each refusal is invalid_arguments; read its field, received and constraints, then change that input. Syntax error: use valid numeric Python; separate statements with actual decoded newlines or semicolons. Do not leave literal backslash-n characters between statements after JSON decoding. Repair and retry the calculation rather than supplying a mental substitute. Imports: remove the import and use the prebound name. Unknown name: pass it in bindings or use a listed helper; variables do not survive calls. Output count/size: select only the small final results with outputs, return a slice/summary, or split independent calculations. Non-finite result: check zero division, scale and units; use geom.unit/angle_deg for directions. Limits: 4096 UTF-8 source bytes, 24 statements, 16 bindings, at most 12 selected outputs and 64 elements per returned value in at most 2 dimensions, ** literal exponent magnitude <=8. No loops, comprehensions, definitions or arbitrary imports. Memory/time exhaustion calls for a smaller calculation, not the identical retry.
replace.geometry_query:
Compute metric geometry from one policy-visible camera's published RGB-D and calibration: project world points to pixels, back-project pixels to world points, or summarise the valid depth of a rectangle.
Use when: a geometric quantity must be derived from calibration rather than estimated from the picture. The clearest case is world_points_m, which is the only way to ask where a world coordinate you already hold falls in an image -- for locating the commanded TCP target, a planned waypoint or a proposal's pregrasp point in the view you are looking at, and for reading whether it is in front of the camera and inside the frame. region answers "how deep is this patch" over a rectangle without naming a pixel. Near miss against mark_point: if you want a pixel measured, kept under a name and re-checked against a complementary view, call mark_point -- it verifies a repeated name across views (a disagreement beyond 25 mm fails that entry), reports depth-support counts and draws the overlay. This tool's points is the same back-projection without the mark, the name, the cross-view check or the image; prefer it when you want the number now and nothing retained, or when the pixel belongs to a saved step rather than the current observation.
Effect: read-only. It does not move the robot, change the scene, consume a robot decision, return any image, or persist a mark or reference; it reads the already-published observation artifacts and their calibration and returns numbers. Every result names the step and the source state it was computed from, and world_points_m additionally names the calibration hash it used.
Returns: exactly one of world_points, points or region_result, alongside step, source_state_sha256 and camera. world_points gives, per requested point, its camera-frame coordinates, in_front, in_frame, and -- when it is in front of the camera -- exact and rounded pixel_uv plus the scene depth already at that pixel and the residual between the two. points gives, per requested pixel, valid plus the median depth, the supporting sample count and world_xyz_m when depth was usable. region_result gives the rectangle, its valid sample count and fraction, and min/median/max depth when any sample was valid.
Does not: identify or segment an object, decide visibility or occlusion, or prove reachability, collision clearance, contact, retention or task success. A positive depth_residual_m means the scene surface at that pixel is nearer than your point, which is evidence of occlusion and not a verdict on it; in_frame is image bounds, not line of sight. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, never an object centre or its hidden extent, and no returned number is simulator ground truth.
On error: Refused: none or two of points, region and world_points_m, with a message naming all three; a camera outside the fixed list; a step that names no saved observation (invalid_arguments, naming the saved range); more than sixteen points or world points, or a non-finite world coordinate; window_px outside 0 to 15; a pixel outside the image, which refuses the whole call rather than its entry; a rectangle that leaves the image or does not have x0<x1 and y0<y1. Use the named view's own top-left OpenCV pixel frame, keep every pixel and the whole rectangle inside that image, and order the rectangle [x0,y0,x1,y1] with x0<x1 and y0<y1. Missing or invalid depth is reported, never inferred, and does not fail the call: a points entry returns valid false with no depth or world_xyz_m, region_result reports valid_count 0 with no depth_m, and a projected world point carries null scene_depth_m and depth_residual_m. To obtain a reading, move the pixel farther inside the intended surface, widen window_px, or read a complementary view. The camera list is fixed: agentview, wrist. The wrist moves with the arm, so its calibration is valid only at the pose it was captured at -- after any motion, query the fresh observation instead of reusing an earlier pixel from it. Adjacent calculation: use compute for arithmetic on already supplied world-frame numbers. Keep projection, back-projection and depth sampling here so they bind the selected observation and calibration.
replace.grasp_plan:
Generate inspectable public RGB-D grasp candidates for one current target.
Use when: current grounding or segmentation identifies the intended object and you need parallel-jaw poses.
Effect: read-only; queries Contact-GraspNet using the selected source-camera RGB-D and compiles poses to the public TCP convention. Optional synchronized views provide review evidence.
Returns: up to three candidates, complete world-frame pregrasp_pose and contact_pose, copyable bounded contact_approach targets, predicted opening, compiler checks and labeled review images. Reachability here is the planning-time IK reference described under IK selection below; move_pose still runs its own admission. Inspect every candidate panel and choose target identity and geometry independently of rank. For this atomic surface, command the selected pregrasp_pose with move_pose, then read the receipt and fresh observation before approaching or closing with set_gripper. Re-plan candidates after any world action. Pose handoff: when manually commanding a returned world pose, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion, then copy position_m and orientation_xyzw unchanged. Send these fields at the top level. Choose interaction by the intended physical contact. Schema example only; replace the illustrative pose with your selected current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}
Does not: plan trajectories, certify reachability, move the robot, command a gripper, use object ground truth, certify retention or report task success. Backend rank is not a success probability. Missing optional review cameras do not invalidate usable primary input.
On error: Refused: a target_ref unknown in this round (target_ref_unavailable) or bound to an earlier observation (stale_observation); max_candidates outside 1 to 3; unusable primary RGB-D or a transient backend failure (grasp_proposal_failed); a request the grasp-proposal service rejects (invalid_arguments, with the service's detail). Not refused but moved to diagnostics.rejected: a candidate whose predicted opening exceeds the 80 mm nominal ceiling, or whose controlled point or pregrasp lies outside the action workspace; with none left the result is status no_candidate. Obtain a better current view or select another target or candidate. Recompute after the target or observation changes. After a submitted motion fails, use its phase and measured residual to choose the next action. Retention evidence remains advisory. IK selection: before the max_candidates display cap, every compiled candidate in a pool of up to 32 is checked with this backend's read-only inverse kinematics -- pregrasp_pose as a free_space pose from the current joints, then contact_pose as a contact_approach pose solved from that pregrasp solution, trying the compiled orientation and then its 180-degree jaw flip about the grip site's local +Z. Candidates it calls reachable are shown first, those whose approach is within 30 degrees of straight down before the rest, each group in backend order; the cap then keeps the first max_candidates and nothing else is dropped. Each shown candidate carries ik_reachability {reachable, member, pregrasp, approach, approach_tilt_from_vertical_deg}, and the result's ik_reachability states the solver, how many pool candidates were checked and how many were reachable. On this backend the solver is one CuRobo IK solve per pose with joint limits and Panda self-collision only (ik_model libero_curobo_ik_robot_only_v1, matches_move_pose_admission false): it knows no table, object or scene and plans no trajectory, and its disagreement with move_pose has not yet been measured. It is an IK reference at planning time, not a guarantee: every motion still runs its own backend admission. reachable null means the check was unavailable and the backend order was kept. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: ik_reachability.claim_boundary is "IK reference at planning time for the compiled pregrasp (free_space from the measured joints) and approach (contact_approach from that pregrasp solution), trying the exact orientation and its 180-degree jaw flip; not a guarantee. Execution runs its own backend check, and any world action stales this.".
replace.mark_point:
Measure up to eight visible pixels of one current RGB view as world-frame points in a single call.
Use when: one or more exact pixels — not an object identity, centre or full extent — must become world XYZ for a waypoint, clearance comparison or geometric fallback. Pass point_ids and points_uv index-aligned and of equal length, in the native top-left [x,y] coordinates of the named view, choosing pixels well inside the intended visible surface. For one pixel, pass one point_id and one points_uv entry in the same batch format.
Effect: read-only with respect to the world, but every measured pixel persists one observation-bound geometric mark under its point_id. Reusing a name already solved from another view verifies the new measurement against the stored one instead of replacing it; a disagreement beyond 25 mm fails only that entry, with error_code inconsistent_mark, and keeps the stored measurement.
Returns: a call status of solved, partial or failed, plus one marks[] entry per requested pixel in request order, each repeating its own source_index. An entry carries its own status, xyz_m in metres when it solved, the distinct views that measured that name, and its depth-support evidence — measured depth, window radius, valid, supporting and rejected sample counts, and maximum support deviation — on success and on failure alike. The call returns one composite overlay: each entry names the colour_rgb it was drawn in, and image_mapping binds a panel to a source_index rather than to its position, because inline images are evicted one block at a time. Measurement feedback states coordinate units and limitations; null residuals are unmeasured.
Does not: track a pixel through robot or camera motion, segment or identify the object, infer hidden geometry, correct a click on the wrong surface, expose simulator ground truth, or prove reachability, collision clearance, contact, retention or success. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, not an object centre, and eight measured pixels are not a shape.
On error: Refused: a call with more than eight entries, point_ids and points_uv of unequal lengths, a repeated or empty name, a name longer than 64 characters, a negative pixel coordinate, or a view that cannot be marked; the whole call is refused and the refusal names the field. A pixel that cannot be measured fails only its own entry and leaves the rest solved. Read that entry's error_code: aim farther inside the surface for depth_discontinuity or insufficient_depth_support, choose a different pixel for invalid_depth at the camera far plane, and resolve a disputed name from a complementary current view. A wrist camera moves with its arm, so after any motion discard old wrist pixels and query the fresh observation rather than hand-projecting the old image location.
replace.move_pose:
Submit a complete pose target through the Supervisor.
Use when: moving the public TCP to a stated position and orientation. This surface drives one right arm: send the target fields directly, with no targets wrapper and no arm choice. Each arm names its two choices as enums -- position_mode (hold_current, absolute, delta) and orientation_mode (hold_current, absolute_quaternion, axis_angle_delta) -- and sends that mode's fields beside them in the arguments themselves. absolute takes position_m; delta takes translation_m and position_frame; absolute_quaternion takes orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta takes rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg and orientation_frame -- rotation_angle_deg is in DEGREES, and no field here takes radians. To hold one half while changing the other, set its mode to hold_current. Label the target free_space, precision or contact_approach by physical intent, not by controller name.
Effect: compiles the request once. free_space uses global CuRobo, then one bounded local OSC settle when the measured endpoint misses by more than 5 mm or 0.05 rad and by no more than 50 mm and 15 degrees. precision within 50 mm and 15 degrees uses bounded OSC; larger precision uses global CuRobo and the same settle. contact_approach within 50 mm and 15 degrees uses bounded OSC. A larger contact_approach is staged: global CuRobo to a pre-contact pose on the way that leaves at most 35 mm and 10 degrees, then bounded OSC for the rest. The local segment runs only after the pre-contact segment converges; otherwise the receipt's precontact field names why, and the arm stays where that segment ended. A failed local route never silently falls back to global.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival, and available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: ask the policy to choose CuRobo versus local OSC; change an exact requested orientation; command a gripper; move an omitted arm; infer contact, retention or task success; retry a failed local stage through another backend.
On error: Refused: an unknown field, a mode without its companion fields or a field of another mode, each naming the field; hold_current for both halves, a target equal to the measured pose, a rotation_angle_deg outside [-180, 180] or an orientation_xyzw whose norm lies outside [0.98, 1.02], each as invalid_motion_arguments without a field; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds) unless the grip site is already outside it and the target only reduces the violation; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). position_mode delta without translation_m is refused at translation_m; a field belonging to another mode is refused by name. planner_failed describes a bounded planner search failure; planning_diagnostics distinguishes target IK convergence/admission from trajectory search when the backend exposes it; plan_rejected means zero controller writes; not_reached means execution started but measured convergence or endpoint verification failed. Use the named phase and fresh evidence rather than repeating the same target blindly. Failure diagnosis: planner_error identifies a failed planner service or implementation, not an unreachable target; invalid_start_state requires correcting the measured start; planner_failed reports ordinary search failure. not_reached preserves endpoint and controller evidence independently of official task termination. Read the fresh observation before proposing another action. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance (also on move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch): the jaw footprint's lowest point at the target (fingers, plus the held object's localized extent when the jaws hold a named target) minus the highest surface the current depth images show beneath it or within radius_m; negative means that surface is higher; occluded surfaces are unknown; not a collision check. The jaws count as holding when the last gripper command was close and the measured jaw separation exceeds 3 mm, which does not confirm a grasp. world_axes compiles approach_world (the grip site's local +Z) and jaw_line_world (its local +X) into orientation_xyzw. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.target_axes_world, on move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch, gives the submitted orientation's world approach and jaw-line directions. Before submission each target gets a read-only reach pre-check, compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.reach_along_request. On this backend it is approximate and is not what move_pose runs: one CuRobo IK solve for the grip site from the measured joints, with joint limits and Panda self-collision only and no table, object or scene model (ik_model libero_curobo_ik_robot_only_v1, matches_move_pose_admission false). move_pose plans a full CuRobo trajectory where it routes globally and moves by bounded OSC, which no IK check models, where it routes locally. Its disagreement with move_pose has not yet been measured (measured_disagreement null). If the target does not solve, it also reports the farthest solving fraction of the straight path from the current pose, and that pose. It never blocks or changes the move. When the target does not solve, reach_along_request also carries nearest_reachable_orientation: the smallest turn of the requested orientation (15 to 75 degrees in 15-degree steps, about axes perpendicular to the approach axis) that the same pre-check solves with the grip site held where the request put it, as a pose with approach_world and tilt_from_straight_down_deg, or none_within_sweep; endpoint IK only, with the pre-check's error. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance.claim_boundary (move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch) is "From the current depth images and their calibration only; points inside the measured jaws, the held object and the space above them are excluded as robot, other robot links are not; occluded surfaces and object undersides are unknown; points up to the footprint's top within radius_m count; not a collision check or a contact prediction, and the move is submitted unchanged."; compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.reach_along_request.claim_boundary is "Read-only IK at sampled points of the straight interpolation from the measured pose to the target; reachability is not proven monotone between samples, and no path, collision, payload or arrival claim. One CuRobo v0.7.8 IK solve per pose by the IK solver of the planner that move_pose's global segment uses, seeded from the measured joints or a chained query's solution, with joint limits and Panda self-collision only: no table, object or scene model. The solution's grip site is checked against the 0.005 m / 0.05 rad arrival bound. It plans no trajectory and does not model the bounded OSC route, so move_pose can still refuse or fail to reach a pose reported reachable, and a pose reported unreachable may still be reachable: the seed search is finite." for an unsolved target and, for a solved one, the same text from "One CuRobo v0.7.8 IK sol" on; reach_along_request.nearest_reachable_orientation.claim_boundary is "Read-only IK at each candidate endpoint by the same reach check as reach_along_request (its ik_model, matches_move_pose_admission and measured_disagreement apply), from the measured joints: the requested orientation turned about axes perpendicular to its approach axis, holding the jaw centre; no path, collision, payload or arrival claim, and an orientation outside the sweep may solve."; last_action_effect.detail.planning_diagnostics.note is "Counts overlap; raw joint bounds do not isolate self-collision or other constraints. World collision model is absent.".
replace.move_to:
Move the right grip site to a world-frame position while holding the measured action-start orientation.
Use when: the intended change is translation-only free-space repositioning and orientation is already suitable.
Effect: world mutation; compiles through canonical move_pose with interaction free_space, so the qualified global CuRobo route executes it, followed by one bounded local OSC settle when the measured endpoint misses by more than 5 mm or 0.05 rad and by no more than 50 mm and 15 degrees. One robot decision.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: rotate, command the gripper, take an arm choice, or guarantee reachability; endpoint arrival does not prove alignment or contact.
On error: Refused: a field other than position_m; a non-finite position; a target equal to the measured position; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds) unless the grip site is already outside it and the target only reduces the violation; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Inspect the named failure stage and residual, pick a reachable intermediate position, or use recover_pose after a genuine motion failure. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. Its compiled_pose targets carry reach_along_request, the same approximate pre-check as move_pose's.
replace.observe:
Inspect current or saved public camera images without moving the world.
Use when: you need named-point overlays or a saved same-round view, including a same-camera retention baseline with step=recovery.baseline_step. Current physical-camera RGB and calibration are already delivered automatically; use those images directly when sufficient. Calling observe does not advance or recapture the world.
Effect: read-only; step selects an immutable observation in the current round, never recaptures or rewinds the environment.
Returns: images, dimensions and actual or actual_historical_observation status; historical results name observation_step.
Does not: establish object identity, attachment or task success; historical images are not the current world.
On error: Refused: an empty or repeated views list or a view outside this tool's enum; history_point_ids naming a mark that is not solved; a step outside the current round's saved steps (invalid_arguments, naming that range); with step, history_point_ids or a point-cloud view. Choose a saved step in the current round. With step, use physical camera views only and omit history_point_ids. For a complementary retention check, inspect the same camera both at baseline and now, then segment each with its matching step. Measurement feedback states coordinate units and limitations; null residuals are unmeasured. Images are explicitly indexed when present. All current physical camera RGB and calibration are delivered automatically before decisions. Depth stays query-based; precise pixel measurements use mark_point. Omitted views selects every physical camera; request a subset only for a specific overlay or historical comparison. Public robot facts: return measured pose, controlled-frame world axes, and measured finger/command state with explicit semantics. Each returned physical camera includes native RGB dimensions, pinhole intrinsics and a world-to-camera CV transform from this exact observation; historical requests use historical calibration. Derived point-cloud panels have no pinhole calibration. Full current camera coverage is supplied automatically. Numerical joint opening alone never proves a grasp; unavailable measurements remain null or explicitly unavailable. Delivered copies leave out what they would only repeat. In public_robot_facts a camera entry omits native_pixel_to_image_offset_xy when it is [0, 0] and image_view when it is that camera's own name; end effectors omit orientation_order and controlled_frame, because every pose is [x, y, z, qx, qy, qz, qw] of the controlled point the embodiment card names. In last_action_effect.detail an arm that was not targeted lists only its non-null fields, and its inactive_arm_drift only above 0.1 mm or 0.01 deg. A claim_boundary, evidence_scope or note whose fixed text a tool's description states is left out of that tool's results and effects.
replace.recover_pose:
Plan the right arm to a named robot-only recovery configuration while preserving the gripper command.
Use when: a planner or execution failure, or a poor configuration, makes ordinary waypoint correction inappropriate; choose previous to return to the joints measured at the start of the last motion action, or home for a deliberate return to the source-bound start configuration.
Effect: world mutation through the qualified global CuRobo recovery route. One robot decision.
Returns: the submitted strategy; the next receipt and fresh observation report actual planning, residuals and preservation evidence. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values.
Does not: reset the episode, restore moved objects or evaluator state, release the gripper, reverse an old trajectory, act as an emergency stop, or guarantee escape from contact.
On error: Refused: a strategy other than previous and home; an unknown field; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). An unavailable recovery state is not a refusal: the receipt reports planner_failed with recovery_state_unavailable; try the other strategy only when physically sensible, otherwise finish with failure honestly. Cost: previous undoes only the last motion action, so the arm travels about as far as that action did (measured median 9 mm on LIBERO); home travels to the start configuration wherever the task stands (measured median 260 mm, about six ordinary pose commands) and gives up the approach already made. Prefer previous when the last motion left a poor configuration; choose home only when the configuration before that motion is unusable too.
replace.report_issue:
Record concise feedback about a tool, observation, or context defect. Use when: the policy encounters an interface or evidence problem worth preserving, not merely normal task difficulty. Effect: read-only with respect to the world and appends one diagnostic record without ending the episode. Returns: an acknowledgement after the diagnostic record is persisted; the Native acknowledgement may contain no additional decision fields.
Does not: repair the issue, change the robot or environment, consume a robot action, determine task success, or finish the episode. On error: Refused: any field other than message, or a message that is empty or only whitespace (invalid_arguments). Shorten the message to one concrete symptom and continue only if the remaining evidence is safe to use.
replace.rotate_pitch:
Tilt the current approach axis while holding position.
Use when: rotating the right grip site about its lateral axis (Panda local +Y) while holding position — for example tilting the approach direction between top-down and side grasps.
Effect: compiles the signed angle to an exact pose through canonical move_pose; rotations of at most 15 degrees execute through the bounded OSC servo, larger ones through global CuRobo and the bounded local settle move_pose describes. One robot decision.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: translate, command the gripper, or prove the new approach direction clears obstacles — verify from a fresh observation.
On error: Refused: an angle outside [-180, 180] degrees or not a finite number; an angle of 0; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds), which includes any rotation while the grip site is already outside it; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Check the current grip-site axes and correct the sign or magnitude; use move_pose when position must change together with orientation. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. Its compiled_pose targets carry reach_along_request, the same approximate pre-check as move_pose's.
replace.rotate_wrist:
Rotate the jaw line around the current approach axis while holding position.
Use when: rotating the right grip site about its approach axis (Panda local +Z, pointing out of the gripper) while holding position — usually to align the jaw-closing line with an object's grasp axis before descending.
Effect: compiles the signed angle to an exact pose through canonical move_pose. Rotations of at most 15 degrees execute through the bounded OSC servo; larger rotations execute through global CuRobo and the bounded local settle move_pose describes. One robot decision.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: expose a literal wrist joint, translate, command the gripper, or verify that the jaws actually align with the object — confirm alignment from a fresh observation.
On error: Refused: an angle outside [-180, 180] degrees or not a finite number; an angle of 0; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds), which includes any rotation while the grip site is already outside it; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Check the current grip-site axes and correct the sign or magnitude; after a substantial rotation re-observe before descending. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. Its compiled_pose targets carry reach_along_request, the same approximate pre-check as move_pose's.
replace.set_gripper:
Set the gripper to a named directive.
Use when: you are opening to release or approach, or closing to grasp, and you already know which directive each gripper should hold. This embodiment has one arm, so the directive needs no arm name. For manual grasp or placement, complete and inspect the required pose action before issuing the gripper-only command; this call does not execute a returned pose or candidate.
Effect: submits one gripper directive per named gripper through the Supervisor and consumes one robot decision. The end-effector pose target is held unchanged. Measured state may still move under contact, and that is evidence rather than a fault.
Returns: a submitted acknowledgement, then a measured receipt and a fresh observation on the next turn. When closing, an intent block echoes the target_ref you supplied and labels it agent_annotation_only.
Does not: prove anything was grasped, held, released or moved; report jaw separation; verify what the jaws closed on; or make target_ref evidence -- it is your annotation of what you believe you are closing on, never a measurement. A closed jaw is not a grasp.
On error: Refused: an action other than open and close; a target_ref that is blank or not a string (invalid_arguments, naming target_ref); the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). A schema refusal is invalid_arguments naming the field; an invalid_motion_arguments refusal names none -- re-read this schema rather than resubmitting the same shape. invalid_arguments naming target_ref means a blank string was sent; send a non-empty reference or omit it entirely. Timing: the simulator advances in 20 Hz control ticks (50 ms each). One command runs until the jaws are within 0.03 of the commanded normalized opening, until they stop moving short of it, or for at most 80 control ticks (4 s). A full close in free air takes about 15 ticks (0.75 s). A close that stops on an object ends as soon as the jaws stop, typically within 0.7 s, and reports not_reached with failure_code gripper_stalled_before_target and gripper_outcome.measured_aperture_mm; that is the expected result of closing on an object, not a controller fault. A stalled close is consistent with a grasp but does not prove one: compare the measured aperture with the object's width, then lift and observe. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: the action effect's gripper_outcome.claim_boundary is "stalled_before_target means the jaws stopped short of the commanded opening; it is consistent with an object between the fingers and is not proof of a grasp".
replace.vision_ground: Retrieve and present up to three inspectable candidate regions for one short text description in the current native-resolution RGB-D observation. Use when: the task names an object or part and the Agent should reduce the scene-level visual search space before making its own semantic identity decision. Effect: read-only with respect to the world and creates separate observation-bound target_ref artifacts for every returned candidate; the service proposes regions but the Agent remains the selection authority. Returns: zero to three ranked candidates with target_ref, backend-local score, bounding box and visible-depth summary, followed by image 0 as the numbered full-scene overview and one labelled 1024x800 raw/mask candidate card per result in T0/T1/T2 order; compare the enlarged raw appearances and select the intended target_ref yourself. Does not: make a black-box semantic decision, certify that any candidate is the named object, add sensor resolution, treat backend score as calibrated probability, expose object ground truth, or prove reachability or grasp success. On error: Refused: max_candidates outside 1 to 3, before any request is sent; text that is empty after trimming or longer than 120 characters; a camera outside this tool's enum; no grounding service (grounding_unavailable); a request the grounding service rejects (invalid_arguments, with the service's detail). Rephrase the visible description to obtain a better candidate set, switch current camera, inspect with observe, or use point-based vision_segment for an instance the Agent can already identify. Selection check: compare the requested task referent with every candidate crop and the original view; rank 0 and a high score do not authenticate identity. Separate an instance hypothesis from an observed property. Failed grasping is not evidence that the intended object is static or that a different object is the target. Revise a mistaken association when the visible evidence contradicts it. Boundary and mask/depth diagnostics describe observability, not semantic truth. Localization also carries a single-view support estimate: support_z_m is the height of the surface the target stands on, fitted to depth pixels just outside its mask and evaluated under it; height_above_support_m is the visible top's height above that surface; mid_height_z_m is the midpoint between them; support_point_count counts the pixels that support the fit, and the three heights are null when no support is visible. center_xyz_m is a visible-surface median, so from an oblique or overhead camera it sits near the top; for a parallel-jaw side grasp, use mid_height_z_m as the height reference instead. The estimate is not ground truth: a neighbouring object, a container wall or a hidden base can bias it. Localization also carries a footprint estimate: footprint_center_xyz_m is the centre of the box that bounds the target's measured outline in its own principal frame (z is the median visible height), footprint_extent_m is that box's two sides, longest first, view_tilt_deg is the angle between the camera-to-target ray and straight down, and footprint_view says whether the view was overhead (at most 20 degrees) or oblique. From an oblique camera only the near side is visible, so center_xyz_m, the AABB and the footprint all sit horizontally toward the camera, by up to half the target's depth; an occluding neighbour can also cut the outline short. From an overhead view the outline is the whole top, and the footprint centre is the target's horizontal centre, handles included. An oblique measurement carries overhead_view_pose: a copyable move_pose target that puts the wrist camera 30 cm above the footprint centre looking straight down, with the current jaw yaw; after that move, run this tool again on the wrist camera and use the overhead footprint_center_xyz_m. Placement: measure the receiving surface from overhead before you grasp, while nothing you hold hides it; measure the object from overhead before grasping and, after the close, keep offset = object footprint centre minus the grip-site position; to set the object on the receiver, send the grip site to the receiver's footprint centre minus that offset (horizontal components), holding the yaw. overhead_view_pose is not a reachability or collision check, and the footprint is not ground truth.
replace.vision_segment:

Use when: comparing plausible regions around the intended object; give 1–8 source-pixel points, usually 3–5 separated interior points. Every point is queried independently, not jointly as one mask prompt, and every point comes back with its own answer.
Effect: world-read-only; binds one current or saved same-round RGB-D view, reuses its image encoding, keeps each point's own SAM alternatives and records immutable masks and per-point query outcomes.
Returns: candidates[] and queries[], one query entry per input point in input order. max_candidates is a PER-POINT budget (default 3, maximum 3): every point's leading mask is admitted before any point's second, so a point that produced a usable mask always keeps one. At most 12 distinct masks and 5 enlarged crops are delivered, and each point reports omitted_over_point_limit and omitted_over_call_cap separately from status no_candidate, which means no mask at that pixel rather than a spent budget. Inspect the proposals and select the intended semantic region.
Does not: require position 0 to be the intended object, prove identity, add sensor resolution by enlargement, mutate the world or grant motion permission. A point on background, boundary or shadow can return the table, robot or a neighbour. Historical pixels never become current geometry after motion.

From an oblique camera only the near side is visible, so center_xyz_m, the AABB and the footprint all sit horizontally toward the camera, by up to half the target's depth; an occluding neighbour can also cut the outline short.
